message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"lekarstwem","gloss":"with/as a medicine (instrumental case of 'lekarstwo')","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"Theuth's clause is 'wynalazek ten jest lekarstwem na pamięć i mądrość', 'this invention is a medicine for memory and wisdom'. 'Na' ('for/against') gives the sense of a cure for a lack."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"pamięć","gloss":"memory","note":"Accusative after 'na' ('for'). The translator also renders μνημονικωτέρους earlier as 'sprawniejszymi w pamiętaniu'."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"mądrość","gloss":"wisdom","note":""},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"lekarstwo","gloss":"medicine, remedy","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"The same lexeme as at 274e, only in the nominative case after 'nie jest'. Thamus then uses a different word, 'środek' (means, device), for what the invention actually is: 'środek na przypominanie sobie'. That second word stands where the Greek has φάρμακον in the second half of the antithesis, so it is the Greek φάρμακον split across two words."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"pamięć","gloss":"memory","note":"Accusative after 'na'. The phrase is 'nie jest lekarstwo na pamięć', 'it is not a medicine for memory'."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"przypominanie sobie","gloss":"reminding oneself, recalling to oneself","note":"A verbal noun with a reflexive pronoun, so 'reminding' is made self-directed. Since it follows 'środek na', the whole phrase reads 'a means for reminding oneself'."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"pozór mądrości","gloss":"appearance/semblance of wisdom","note":"Contrasted with 'mądrość prawdziwą', 'true wisdom'. This is a wording of 'doxa' as 'appearance', and it does not mean 'reputation' or 'opinion'. The Greek 'alētheia' is rendered by the adjective 'prawdziwą', 'true'."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"mędrcy z pozoru","gloss":"sages from appearance, i.e. apparent sages","note":"The compound is split into a noun plus a prepositional phrase. It is followed by 'a nie ludzie mądrzy naprawdę', 'and not people wise in truth'. It echoes 'pozór' from the earlier line."},"argument":"Witwicki keeps one word, 'lekarstwo', for both occurrences of pharmakon in the first half of the antithesis, so Thamus does throw Theuth's own word back at him: 'not a lekarstwo for memory'. For the positive half he switches to 'środek na przypominanie', a neutral 'means', so the Greek second pharmakon is rendered by a different, less medical word. This keeps the medicine image in the denial but loses it in the affirmation, and the reply reads more as a correction of purpose than as a reversal of the drug's effect. The doxa vocabulary ('pozór', 'z pozoru') is kept consistent, which makes the opposition between appearance and truth clear."}
